records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — The attendee rows are committed before the calendar update, so a calendar failure leaves guests persisted but unsynced and a retry rejects them as existing.
records.rationale: The diff shows in addGuests.handler.ts that prisma.booking.update (lines 85-99) creates the attendee records in the database first, then eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is called later (line 161). If the calendar update fails, the attendees are already persisted in the database. On retry, the uniqueGuests filter (lines 68-72) will exclude these emails since they now exist in booking.attendees

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167 — Email delivery failures are swallowed, causing the mutation to report success although the newly added guests may never be notified.
records.rationale: The diff shows at line 167-169 in addGuests.handler.ts that email failures are caught and only logged with console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails'), then the function returns success with { message: 'Guests added' }. This is a real concern - the mutation reports success even when guests weren't notified. However, this is a design decision rather than a bug - the guests ARE added to the databas

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any authenticated attendee can add arbitrary email addresses to a booking and receive its calendar/video details without organizer approval.
records.rationale: The diff shows in addGuests.handler.ts lines 47-52 that any authenticated user who is an attendee (isAttendee check at line 49) can add guests to a booking. The permission check at lines 51-53 allows access if isAttendee is true, meaning any existing attendee can add arbitrary email addresses as guests.
